mainTopic: The limits of רקב, the decayed dust of a corpse: outside matter mixed in, a ground-up corpse, a corpse missing a part, and decay that began during life.
overview: The גמרא finishes a list of questions about whether things found with a corpse, such as semen, food waste, skin, phlegm and spittle, count as part of the body or as outside matter that turns its רקב into גלגלין. רב שמואל בר אחא objects that if all of these spoil the dust, טמא רקב could never exist. The גמרא answers with a body that was completely cleaned out inside and out. אביי teaches that a ground-up corpse has no רקב. Whether a corpse that was ground and then decayed has רקב ends in תיקו. עולא בר חנינא teaches that a corpse missing a part has no רקב, no תפוסה and no שכונת קברות. A משנה comparing a מת to a חי is used twice: once to challenge עולא בר חנינא and once to answer רבא's question about a limb that decayed during life. Both times the גמרא answers that the משנה only contrasts the general categories. Finally רבא asks about eating an ant that is missing a part.

steps.title: Semen inside a dead woman's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether semen inside a dead woman counts as part of her body or as outside matter that mixes with her רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about semen inside a woman's womb? Do we say it is like her own body, since no baby formed from it? Or maybe it is not, since it came from outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about semen found inside a dead woman. Does it count as part of her body, or is it an outside substance that mixes with her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רקב is only טמא when it comes purely from the body; outside material mixed in makes גלגלין. One side says the semen never became a fetus, so it just blends into her body. The other side says it came from someone else, so it is outside matter.

keyTerms.meaning: semen
a woman's womb (literally, her insides)
was formed (into a fetus)
it comes from outside
what is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the questions. The גמרא is not asking whether the semen is טמא. It is asking whether it counts as part of the body, which decides whether the dust stays pure רקב or becomes a mixture (גלגלין).

phrases.english: Semen inside a woman's womb, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The woman here has died; the question is about her body turning into רקב.

phrases.english: Do we say: since no fetus was formed from it,
it is considered like her own body,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּמֵעָלְמָא קָאָתֵי — לָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps, since it comes from outside, it is not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of questions about what counts as part of the corpse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does semen inside a dead woman count as her body, or as outside matter that mixes in with her רקב?

steps.title: Food waste inside the body
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks the same kind of question about the food waste left in a dead woman's intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: what about her excrement? Since a person cannot live without eating, maybe it is part of her life. Or maybe this too comes from outside?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a similar question, this time about leftover food waste inside the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food is needed to stay alive, so maybe it counts as part of the living person. But food also clearly comes from outside the body, like the semen in the last step.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (a question)
her excrement, the food waste inside her
her life, what keeps her alive

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked: her excrement, what is the law?
Since she cannot survive without eating,
it is her life,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא הָא נָמֵי מֵעָלְמָא אָתֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps this too comes from outside?
phrases.notes: "Too" points back to the semen in the last step, which also came from outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question built the same way as step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the food waste inside the body part of the person (since it keeps her alive), or outside matter?

steps.title: The corpse's skin
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא asks whether a corpse's skin counts as part of the body for רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא asked: what about its skin?
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds one more item to the list of questions: the corpse's skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא gives no reasons here; it simply asks. Skin is part of the body, yet it may not be treated like flesh, sinews and bones, so it is unclear whether it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: its skin

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, asked:
its skin, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: עוֹרוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the series of questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a corpse's skin form a mixture (גלגלין) with its רקב?

steps.title: Phlegm and spittle
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח asks about the corpse's phlegm and spittle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח asked: what about its phlegm and its spittle?
steps.whatsHappening: One last question in the list: do the body's phlegm and saliva count as part of it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are fluids the body itself makes, but they are not flesh, sinews or bones. So the question is whether they count as body or as extra matter. This finishes the list that the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: its phlegm
its spittle, saliva

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoaḥ asked:
its phlegm and its spittle, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ: כִּיחוֹ וְנִיעוֹ מַהוּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do phlegm and spittle form a mixture (גלגלין) with the רקב?

steps.title: If all these spoil it, when is there ever רקב?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אחא challenges רב פפא: if all these things make a mixture, there could never be a case of רקב that is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אחא said to רב פפא: If you think all these things are a mixture, how could you ever find רקב that makes things טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר אחא challenges the whole line of questions. If each of these things ruins the רקב, then רקב could never happen in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every body has food waste, skin, phlegm and similar things inside it. If all of them count as outside matter that creates גלגלין, every corpse would turn into a mixture. Then the law of רקב that is טמא would never apply.

keyTerms.meaning: if it enters your mind, if you think
a mixture of outside matter that stops the dust from being pure רקב
the decayed dust of a corpse, which can be טמא
how would you ever find it?

steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to show that the law of רקב is still possible, even if the questions above are answered strictly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Aḥa said to Rav Pappa:
But if it enters your mind
that all these things they spoke of are a mixture,
how would you ever find רקב that makes things impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כׇּל הָנֵי דְּקָאָמַר הָוֵי גַּלְגַּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind all the questions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that all the substances listed above count as גלגלין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every corpse has these things, so the law of רקב would never apply in practice.

steps.title: A body that was fully cleaned out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with an extreme case: the person was given a strong laxative and a hair remover, and was boiled in the hot springs of טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, when he was given palm water to drink, rubbed with a hair remover, and boiled in the waters of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רקב can still happen. It describes a body where every questionable substance was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The palm water cleans out the intestines. The hair remover takes off the hair, and boiling in hot water removes the skin. What is left is only flesh, sinews and bones, so the רקב would surely be טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: palm water, a strong laxative
rubbed him with a hair-removing substance
boiled him
the hot springs of טבריא

phrases.english: Where they gave him palm water to drink,
phrases.notes: This was done before he died, to empty out his insides.

phrases.english: and rubbed him with a hair remover,
and boiled him in the waters of Tiberias.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a special case where the challenge does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every corpse contains outside matter, so רקב can never be טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A body fully cleaned out inside and outside leaves pure body matter, so its רקב can be טמא.
steps.whatToRemember: The questions about semen, waste, skin and spittle stay open. Even if all of them make גלגלין, רקב is still possible in a body that was completely cleaned out.

steps.title: A ground-up corpse has no רקב
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that a corpse that was ground up does not have the law of רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that a corpse that was ground up has no רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new topic: if a corpse was ground into small pieces, its dust is not counted as רקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רקב comes from a body decaying naturally in the grave. Grinding is not decay, so the result is not רקב. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: we have a tradition, we hold
ground it up

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
A corpse that one ground up has no law of רקב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about רקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A corpse that was ground up does not produce רקב.

steps.title: Ground up, then it decayed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a corpse was ground up and then decayed, is it רקב? Maybe it is, since flesh, sinews and bones are there. Or maybe not, since it did not decay in its original form.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if it was ground and then decayed, what is the law? Is the reason only that there should be flesh, sinews and bones, and here they are? Or maybe we need it to decay in its original form, and that is missing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on אביי's rule. It asks about a corpse that was ground up first and only afterward decayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רקב only needs flesh, sinews and bones, this decayed corpse qualifies. But if רקב needs the body to decay as a whole body, grinding ruined that, and later decay does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among them
and it decayed
flesh, sinews and bones
in its original form, as it was made

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If one ground it, and afterward it decayed, what is the law?
Is the reason anything other than
that there are flesh, sinews and bones, and here they are present.
Or perhaps we need it in its original form, and that is not the case here?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: טְחָנוֹ וְחָזַר וְהִרְקִיב, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a harder case that builds on אביי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רקב only need flesh, sinews and bones, or does it need the body to decay in its original whole form?

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot find an answer, so it leaves the question unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of step 8 stay possible. We do not know whether a corpse that was ground and then decayed produces רקב.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A ground-up corpse has no רקב. If it decayed after being ground up, the question stays unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 8 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is unresolved whether a corpse that was ground and then decayed produces רקב.

steps.title: A corpse missing a part loses three special laws
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר חנינא teaches that a מת שחסר has no רקב, no תפוסה, and no שכונת קברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר חנינא taught: A corpse that is missing a part does not have the law of רקב, nor the law of תפוסה, nor the law of שכונת קברות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from עולא בר חנינא: if a corpse is missing a part, three special טומאה-related laws do not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three laws only apply to a complete corpse. רקב is decayed remains that are טמא in the amount of a full ladle. תפוסה is the soil around a body that is treated as part of it. שכונת קברות is the rule that finding three bodies may mean the area is a graveyard. A missing part takes away all three.

keyTerms.meaning: A corpse that is missing a part
Decayed remains of a corpse, which are טמא in the amount of a full ladle
The earth around a body that is 'caught' with it and treated as part of the corpse
A graveyard area; the rule that finding three bodies may mean the place was a cemetery

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the base rule that the rest of this section challenges and defends.

phrases.english: Ulla bar Ḥanina taught:
A corpse that is missing a part —
does not have the law of decayed remains
nor the law of 'caught' earth
phrases.notes: The soil around the body, which normally has to be moved together with it.

phrases.english: nor the law of a graveyard area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the תיקו about a ground-up corpse; it still deals with the limits of רקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מת שחסר has no רקב, no תפוסה, and no שכונת קברות.

steps.title: A משנה suggests even one decayed limb of a corpse has רקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה comparing a מת to a חי, and reads it as showing that even one decayed limb of a corpse has רקב. That contradicts עולא בר חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a משנה: 'No. You may say this about a corpse, which has the laws of a majority, a quarter-קב, or a full ladle of רקב. Can you say the same about a living person, who has no majority, no quarter-קב, and no full ladle of רקב?' What is the case? It must be that one limb of the living person decayed. So in the matching case of a corpse, even one limb would have רקב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא בר חנינא with a משנה. It reads the משנה as saying that a corpse with just one decayed limb still has רקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts a living person, who has no רקב, with a corpse, which does. The case of a living person can only be one decayed limb. So the matching corpse case also seems to be one limb, which is far from a complete body. That means a part of a corpse, not a whole one, would have רקב, against עולא בר חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: A majority of the body or bones, and a quarter-קב of bones; amounts of a corpse that make things טמא
A full ladle, the amount of רקב that makes things טמא
What is the case? What are the circumstances?

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself never says a single limb of a corpse has רקב. That idea is an inference the גמרא draws from the comparison, and the next step attacks exactly that.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
No. If you say this about a corpse,
which has the laws of a majority and a quarter-kav
or a full ladle of decayed remains —
would you say the same about a living person,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לֹא רוֹב, וְלֹא רוֹבַע,
phrases.english: who does not have the law of a majority, nor a quarter-kav,
nor a full ladle of decayed remains?!
What is the case? That one limb decayed,
so in the matching case with a corpse:
even one limb has the law of decayed remains!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא בר חנינא's rule from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא בר חנינא's rule that a מת שחסר has no רקב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's comparison suggests that a corpse with only one decayed limb (a partial corpse) still has רקב.

steps.title: The משנה only speaks about the general category of a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה never says this one-limb corpse has רקב. It only teaches that a corpse in general has רקב and a living person in general does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the משנה say that this corpse (with one limb) has רקב? No. It is teaching us this: the category of 'corpse' has רקב, and the category of 'living person' does not have רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא בר חנינא by saying the challenge read too much into the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not comparing one case to another case. It is comparing two categories: a corpse can have רקב (when it is whole), while a living person never can. So nothing in the משנה says a partial corpse has רקב, and עולא בר חנינא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach that? (pointing out the source never said it)
This is what it is teaching us
The name or category of something

steps.whatToRemember: A מת שחסר has no רקב. The משנה only means that the category of מת has רקב, while the category of חי never does.

phrases.english: Does it teach that this corpse has it?
This is what it teaches us:
the category of a corpse has decayed remains,
the category of a living person does not have decayed remains.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָתָנֵי הָא מֵת? הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the comparison is between categories, not specific cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה compares a one-limb case in a living person with a one-limb case in a corpse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only contrasts the category of מת (which has רקב) with the category of חי (which does not), so עולא בר חנינא's rule stands.

steps.title: רבא asks about a limb that decayed before death
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if a limb decayed while the person was alive and then he died, does the body have רקב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If a limb decayed while the person was alive, and then he died, what is the law? Maybe the tradition of רקב only applies when the body decayed after death. Or maybe, since he is dead now in any case, it counts as רקב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question about a body whose decay started while the person was still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the tradition of רקב is about a body that decayed as a corpse, so decay from life makes it like a מת שחסר with no רקב. The other side says what matters is the present: he is dead now, so his remains count as רקב.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question with two sides)
We have a tradition (a law received by tradition)
Or perhaps
Now, in any case

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If a limb decayed while he was alive,
and then he died, what is the law?
When we have the tradition of decayed remains,
it is only where it decayed when he was dead.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא הָא מָיֵית?
phrases.english: Or perhaps, now at any rate, he is dead?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a מת שחסר has no רקב and asks whether decay from life counts as 'missing'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does decay that began during life stop the remains from being רקב after death, or does the present state of death decide?

steps.title: Trying to answer רבא from the משנה about a corpse and a living person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that contrasts a מת with a חי. It infers that the only reason there is no רקב is that the person is alive, so once he dies the body would have רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'No. If you say this about a corpse, which has rules of a majority, a quarter-קב, and a full ladle of decayed matter, would you say it about a living person?' The reason is that he is alive. So a dead person has רקב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof to answer רבא's question from step 13. It quotes the same משנה from step 11 and draws an inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a living person does not have the rules of רקב. The גמרא reads this as saying the only thing stopping רקב is that the person is alive. So once he dies, the body should have רקב, even though the limb decayed while he was still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the body or bones, and a quarter-קב of bones: amounts of a corpse that make things טמא
A full ladle of the decayed matter of a corpse
The reason

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה the גמרא used in step 11. It is quoted again for a new purpose: this time to answer רבא's question, not to challenge עולא בר חנינא.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
No, if you said this regarding a corpse
which has rules of a majority and a quarter-kav
and a full ladle of decayed matter,
would you say so regarding a living person, etc.
The reason is because he is alive,
which means a corpse does have רקב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question from step 13
steps.raayaObject: That a body which lost a limb while alive does have רקב after death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה contrasting a מת with a חי, read by inference: the only reason there is no רקב is that the person is alive

steps.title: Pushing off the proof: the משנה speaks only in general
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The משנה never says 'but a corpse' about this case. It only teaches that corpses in general have רקב and living people in general do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'but a corpse'? This is what it teaches us: the category of a corpse has רקב, and the category of a living person has no רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 14 with the same answer it gave in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on reading 'but a dead person has רקב' into the משנה for this exact case. The גמרא says the משנה never says that. It only sets up a general contrast between corpses and living people, so רבא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach this? The גמרא is pointing out that the source never says it
This is what it is teaching us
Literally 'the name of': here it means the general category

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה only teaches a general rule: a corpse has רקב and a living person does not. It cannot answer what happens with a limb that decayed during life.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'but a corpse'?
This is what it teaches us:
that the category of a corpse has רקב,
and the category of a living person has no רקב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה for רבא's question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference reads a specific case into the משנה, but the משנה only teaches the general categories of מת and חי

steps.title: רבא asks about an ant that is missing a part
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the law is for an ant that is missing a part. Is the rule based on a set size, which this ant lacks, or on being a whole creature, which it still is?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: An ant that is missing a part, what is the law? Do we have a tradition that the rule is a measurement, and this one is lacking? Or do we have a tradition that the rule is a whole creature, and here there is one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question that is related to the topic of a body missing a part. He sets out two possible ways to think about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a whole ant counts even if it is very small, because it is a complete creature (בריה). רבא asks whether that rule works like a set size, which a missing part would spoil. Or does it depend on the ant still being a creature, which it still is even without the part?

keyTerms.meaning: Asked: a real question the גמרא tries to answer
Ant
A set measurement or amount
A complete creature, which counts even if it is smaller than the usual amount
We have a tradition (we learned it as a received teaching)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
An ant that is missing a part, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is talking about someone who eats it. A whole ant counts as a creature even though it is tiny.

phrases.english: Do we have a tradition about it as a measurement
and this one is lacking?
Or do we have a tradition about it as a whole creature
